title: keybord managment programming with shift doesn't works

status.label: Needs layout-specific repro
status.detail: The screenshots and comment describe working and failing Shift combinations on a non-US keyboard, but the active Windows layout and an isolated result with Keyboard Manager disabled are not confirmed.

next_action: Request the active Windows keyboard layout and one failing mapping's result with Keyboard Manager disabled.

judgment.rationale: The author reports that several remappings work, including Shift+number and Shift+period, while Shift combinations for other punctuation positions do not produce the intended characters. The discussion already contains mapping examples and screenshots, so those should not be requested again. The active Windows layout and the result for one exact failing mapping with Keyboard Manager disabled would distinguish a remap-translation issue from layout or device behavior.
evidence: The open issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, Needs-Team-Response, and Product-Keyboard Manager; it has no assignee.
The body reports PowerToys 0.78 and describes Shift+à and Shift+ù not producing the requested characters.
The author identifies a Ziyoulang K3 keyboard and says other key-to-key, Shift+number, and Shift+period mappings work; the failing list includes Shift with punctuation keys.
The author already provided several mapping examples and four screenshots in the 2024-02-02 comments; no new screenshot request is needed.
The 2026-10-11 activity only changes product labels; there is no newer reproduction or linked pull request.

At upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769, KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:414-420 looks up a single-key mapping by the received virtual-key code, and common/Helpers.cpp:179-195 injects the mapped virtual key with a scan code from MapVirtualKey. The issue's layout-specific failure is not established by this code path alone.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the active Windows layout and a controlled result for one already-described failing Shift mapping before proposing a layout-aware code change.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys remapping issue is plausible, but the exact mapping/layout combination and whether the same physical input behaves normally without Keyboard Manager are still unknown.

issue_context.summary: Some Shift-plus-punctuation mappings on the author's non-US keyboard do not produce the programmed characters, while several neighboring mappings work.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.78 and a Ziyoulang K3 mechanical keyboard.
The author reports that Shift+number and Shift+period mappings work, while Shift with several punctuation-position keys does not.
The author supplied mapping examples and screenshots in the 2024-02-02 discussion.
The current issue has four public comments, no assignee, and no new reproduction after the 2026-10-11 label update.
inferences: Keyboard layout translation or the distinction between physical key position and virtual-key identity may be relevant, but the active layout is not stated.
The differing behavior among keys could indicate a layout-specific mapping path, but the current evidence does not establish a PowerToys defect.
issue_context.analysis: The existing screenshots and examples should be retained as evidence rather than requested again. The next discriminator is whether one failing physical key plus Shift produces the expected character when Keyboard Manager is disabled, along with the active Windows layout. Current source remaps virtual keys and derives scan codes from the target key; it does not prove which layout behavior the author observed.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body, all four comments, labels, assignees, and the complete timeline through 2026-10-11T16:48:58Z.
Confirmed that the author already supplied multiple mapping examples and four screenshots; no linked PR was found.

Read current upstream source at 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769: src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:414-420 and src/modules/keyboardmanager/common/Helpers.cpp:179-195.

information_gaps.information: The active Windows keyboard layout and one exact failing source-key-plus-Shift mapping with its expected target character.
information_gaps.why_needed: The same physical key can resolve to different virtual keys and characters under different layouts.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the Windows input-language/layout name and one source key plus Shift -> configured target from the existing mapping list; do not re-upload the screenshots.

information_gaps.information: Whether that same physical key plus Shift produces the expected character when Keyboard Manager is disabled, and whether the failure occurs in a plain text editor.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates a PowerToys remapping regression from keyboard firmware, layout translation, or application-specific behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Using the same layout and physical keyboard, test the one failing combo with Keyboard Manager off and in a plain text editor, then report the actual character.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve layout-dependent Shift behavior in key remappings
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a remapping based on virtual-key identity and injected target key may not preserve the intended shifted character for some non-US layout positions. The issue does not yet establish whether this is caused by PowerToys or by the active layout/device.
plan: Confirm the Windows layout, exact source and target mapping, and behavior with Keyboard Manager disabled using one failing punctuation key.
Reproduce with that mapping on current main and trace the low-level virtual key and injected target while Shift is held.
If the remapper loses the intended Shift/layout translation, make the smallest targeted correction and add regression coverage for the failing and neighboring working punctuation mappings.
verification: The confirmed source-plus-Shift mapping produces the requested character with Keyboard Manager enabled and does not change the disabled control result.
Existing Shift+number, Shift+period, and unshifted key mappings continue to produce their configured outputs.

confidence.rationale: The report is detailed and includes screenshots, but the active layout and behavior with Keyboard Manager disabled are not supplied, so the failing mechanism remains uncertain.

actions.label: Approve layout-specific remap investigation
actions.note: Proceed to a code design only after the controlled layout and disabled-remap result identify a PowerToys failure.

actions.label: Request keyboard layout and control result

comment.body:
Thanks for the mapping examples and screenshots already attached. To distinguish a PowerToys remap issue from layout translation, could you share:
- The active Windows keyboard layout and one exact failing source key plus Shift -> configured target from the mappings already shown (no need to re-upload screenshots).
- The actual character from that same physical combo with Keyboard Manager disabled, and whether it also fails in a plain text editor.
